subject: using shiny to visualize the best deals on diamonds

messages.author: e569f9ca5b5a4235
messages.subject: using shiny to visualize the best deals on diamonds
parts:
Hi all, it's been a while since I last posted to this group.  I use shiny quite a bit in my personal projects as it's the only I can make data interactive.  I wanted to show off one of my more recent visualizations:

http://www.sproutworkshop.com/diamond-deals/

I've collected diamond prices from James Allen and calculated the cost-efficiency frontier to find the most cost-effective diamonds.  If you're in the market for an engagement ring or know someone who is, I think this will help you find the best deal online.  I have a lot of fun playing with it to see how different diamonds are priced.  Shiny is the perfect name for a diamond app.

Thanks RStudio, for making this possible.

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Re: using shiny to visualize the best deals on diamonds
parts:
This is a very cool decision support app!  Nice work.

It reminded me a lot of the "Tradeoff Analytics" widget that's part of IBM's Watson set of services (http://www.ibm.com/smarterplanet/us/en/ibmwatson/developercloud/tradeoff-analytics.html) which also calculates an efficient frontier and then has a useful visualization of the results.

This leads me to wonder:  Has anyone built anything similar to "Tradeoff Analytics" in R?  
(I've seen a somewhat-unmaintained version of "RadViz" (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/29454321/radviz-survey-permutation-matrix-plots-in-r), but that's all.)
